examples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}+2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t-5)\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its displacement from $t=1$ to $t=4$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(1)&=3\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(4)&=18\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

Subtract the earlier position from the later position.

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(4)-\underset{\sim}{r}(1)&=(18-3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(7-(-2))\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=15\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=8\cos t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+8\sin t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its displacement from $t=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to $t=\pi$, and the exact distance between these positions.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=3t\underset{\sim}{i}+(12-t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its displacement from $t=2$ to $t=5$ and its direction, measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis to the nearest degree.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+5t\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Its displacement from $t=1$ to a later time $T$ is $35\underset{\sim}{i}+25\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $T$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(1)&=\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(T)&=\underset{\sim}{r}(1)+35\underset{\sim}{i}+25\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=36\underset{\sim}{i}+30\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

Compare the horizontal components.

$\begin{aligned}T^{2}&=36\\T&=6\end{aligned}$

Since $T>1$, the negative root is excluded. The vertical component agrees: $5(6)=30$.

examples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+3t\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Its displacement from $t=a$ to $t=a+3$ is $33\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find the two times.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(a+3)-\underset{\sim}{r}(a)&=\big((a+3)^{2}-a^{2}\big)\underset{\sim}{i}+\big(3(a+3)-3a\big)\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=(6a+9)\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

Compare the horizontal components.

$\begin{aligned}6a+9&=33\\6a&=24\\a&=4\end{aligned}$

The vertical component is already $9$, as required. The two times are $t=4$ and $t=7$.

examples.derivation: Independent substitution gives r(1)=(3,-2) and r(4)=(18,7). Later minus earlier gives displacement (15,9), agreeing with the answer. A diagram is unnecessary for this direct component calculation.

At pi/6 the position is (4sqrt(3),4); at pi it is (-8,0). The displacement is (-8-4sqrt(3),-4). Its squared magnitude is 64+64sqrt(3)+48+16=128+64sqrt(3), giving exact distance 8sqrt(2+sqrt(3)). The solution diagram places both endpoints on the radius-8 circle, directs the chord from the earlier to the later position, and distinguishes that displacement from the anticlockwise circular path.

Substitution gives r(2)=(6,8) and r(5)=(15,-13), so displacement is (9,-21). Its reference angle is arctan(21/9)=66.801409... degrees. The fourth-quadrant anticlockwise direction is 293.198590... degrees, rounding to 293 degrees. The translated diagram vector (1.5,-3.5) is proportional to (9,-21); its component annotations and clockwise reference-angle arc agree.

The starting position is (1,5). Adding displacement (35,25) gives final position (36,30). Thus T^2=36 and 5T=30. The later-time requirement selects T=6, and both components agree. No diagram is needed.

The displacement over the three-unit interval is ((a+3)^2-a^2,3(a+3)-3a)=(6a+9,9). Equating horizontal components gives 6a+9=33, hence a=4. The times are 4 and 7, both within the domain. Their positions are (16,12) and (49,21), whose difference is (33,9). No diagram is needed.
